clock_cache_policy: Record timing method, device/software and warm/cold/cache behavior with each actual experiment; use a common setup policy across planner versions.
costs: The helper reports model-transport estimates only, with an amount, currency and recorded pricing/estimation basis per attempt. It does not establish billed charges, cost-free local compute, or full-workflow cost. Non-model retrieval/lookup/provider charges need a separate inventory. Never combine currencies; do not impute unknown costs as zero.
execution_only: Returned means the workflow returned, not that its plan passed independent scoring. Successful-response latency requires a later join to independent outcomes; preserve failed/timeout times separately.
model_usage_unit: One workflow job per call/attempt inventory. A transport attempt has one declared logical-call parent. Additional attempts on that parent count as retries; substantive revision calls have their own logical IDs.
resource_measurements: The later runner records available device/resource observations with metric, unit, device, measurement window and method. Missing GPU, RAM, energy, pricing or token telemetry remains unavailable. No resource probe or estimated utilization is run here.
resumption: The later runner must log run segments, active workflow timing, and any paused/offline interval separately under a frozen policy. Do not mix incompatible clock origins or reconstruct resumed wall time from a last-call duration.
roles_and_phases: Roles (generator/coordinator/specialist/evaluator) and phases (initial/revision) are separate overlapping breakdowns of the same logical calls. Do not add them together. Revision rounds count distinct declared model-call revision indices; non-model revision work needs its own stage observations.
stages: Stage durations can overlap or nest. Keep original IDs/observations; do not sum them into elapsed wall time. Common clock scope and instrumentation must be established by the runner.
startup: Record common startup/model-loading separately. If lazy loading happens inside a request timer it remains part of that request time and must not be subtracted. Startup observations are not added to the recorded request total.
summary_policy: Observed means/totals include available measurements only, with measured/missing counts. Complete totals/means stay null until the declared job inventory is terminal and all expected measurements are available. Pending/unrecorded jobs are unfinished work. Empty latency groups have no numerical latency.
summary_scopes: Retrieval/lookup count aggregates refer to terminal jobs only; pending-job count observations remain in their original records. Stage and startup observation counts describe all recorded jobs. Output scope labels identify this distinction; complete totals remain unavailable while jobs are pending.
tokens: Account input/output token usage once at transport-attempt level, including failures where usage is known. No logical-call token fields or sum of both levels. Missing usage remains null; observed partial totals carry availability counts.
usage_completion: Call and attempt inventories must be complete, attempts terminal, and each declared call represented by an attempt before complete usage totals are exposed. Failed/timeout attempts retain measured usage. Explicit zero counts/tokens are valid for a complete empty inventory.
workflow_timer: One observed whole-workflow request duration includes retrieval/lookup, orchestration, model calls, transport retries, revisions and in-request waiting. It is not reconstructed from the final call or a sum of stage durations.
